title_en: Decision of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on Strengthening the Review and Supervision of the Central Budget

articles.content_en:
I. Strengthening comprehensive review and whole-process oversight. The National People's Congress and its Standing Committee shall conduct comprehensive review and whole-process oversight of government budgets and final accounts, adhere to the centralized and unified leadership of the Party Central Committee, focus on serving the overall work of the Party and the state, take the people as the center, conduct review and oversight according to law, focus on key points, emphasize practical results, ensure the implementation of the Constitution and laws, and ensure the implementation of the state's policies, decisions, and arrangements.
(1) Strengthening review and oversight of fiscal policies. The key points of review and oversight include: the implementation of state policies, decisions, and arrangements by fiscal policies; the alignment with economic and social development goals and the overall requirements of macro-control; the enhancement of medium-term fiscal planning management and the guarantee of major national strategic tasks; the full solicitation of opinions and suggestions from deputies to the National People's Congress and all sectors of society during the formulation of fiscal policies; and the reasonableness, feasibility, and sustainability of fiscal policies.
(2) Strengthening review and oversight of general public budgets. The key points of review and oversight of the total amount and structure of general public budget expenditures include: the implementation of state policies, decisions, and arrangements by the total amount and structure of expenditures; the total amount of expenditures and its increase or decrease, the size of the fiscal deficit and its proportion to the annual estimated gross domestic product; the adjustment and optimization of the expenditure structure, strict control over general expenditures, and improvement of the efficiency of fiscal fund allocation and use performance.
The key points of review and oversight of key expenditures and major investment projects include: the alignment of key expenditure budgets with expenditure policies; changes in the scale and optimization of the structure of key expenditures; the decision-making justification, policy objectives, and performance of key expenditures. The alignment of major investment projects with the national economic and social development plan; the decision-making justification, investment arrangement, and implementation effects of major investment projects.
The key points of review and oversight of departmental budgets include: the inclusion of all revenues and expenditures of each department into the budget; the alignment and matching of departmental budgets with expenditure policies and departmental functions; the construction of project pools; the budget arrangements and performance of key departmental projects; the allocation of new assets; the use of carry-over funds; and the rectification and implementation of issues identified in audits.
The key points of review and oversight of central-to-local transfer payments include: the guarantee by various types of transfer payments of the fiscal powers and expenditure responsibilities borne by the central finance; the promotion of balanced financial resources among regions and the enhancement of the capacity of basic public services at the grassroots level; the improvement and standardization of the transfer payment system and optimization of the transfer payment structure; the periodic evaluation and withdrawal of special transfer payments; the issuance and use of transfer payment budgets; and the performance of transfer payments.
The key points of review and oversight of general public budget revenues include: the adaptation of budget revenue arrangements to economic and social development goals and the overall requirements of national macro-control; the coordination of various tax revenues with corresponding tax bases; the collection of budget revenues in accordance with laws and regulations, and their truthfulness and completeness; the optimization of the budget revenue structure and improvement of quality; and the management of non-tax revenues according to law.
(3) Strengthening review and oversight of government debt. The key points of review and oversight of central government debt include: scientifically determining the balance limit of national debt for the current year based on the central fiscal deficit scale and the balance limit of national debt at the end of the previous year, and reasonably controlling the difference between the balance and the limit of national debt; assessing the level of government debt risk, and promoting the long-term balance between stable growth and risk prevention. The key points of review and oversight of local government debt include: the inclusion of local government debt into budget management; assessing the level of local government debt risk based on indicators such as debt ratio and interest expenditure ratio, and reviewing the reasonableness of the new general debt limit and special debt limit for local governments; the repayment of local government special debt; and the active and steady resolution of local government debt risks.
(4) Strengthening review and oversight of government-managed fund budgets. The key points of review and oversight include: the establishment, collection, use, and duration of fund projects in compliance with laws and regulations; the reasonableness, feasibility, and sustainability of revenue and expenditure policies and budget arrangements; the use of government-managed fund expenditures; and the performance, evaluation, and adjustment of government-managed fund projects.
(5) Strengthening review and oversight of state capital management budgets. The key points of review and oversight include: the completeness of the budget scope and standardized systems; the full contribution of state capital income and income from property rights transfers; the compliance of expenditure use directions and projects with laws, regulations, and policies; the transfer of state capital management budgets into general public budgets; the management of government investment funds; and the optimization of the layout of state capital and alignment with the reform of state-owned assets and enterprises.
(6) Strengthening review and oversight of social insurance fund budgets. The key points of review and oversight include: the arrangement of revenues and expenditures of various funds, fiscal subsidies, and budget balance; the implementation of social security policies through budget arrangements; the promotion of national pooling of basic old-age insurance; fund performance and operational investment; and medium- and long-term revenue and expenditure forecasts and sustainable operation.
(7) Further promoting the disclosure of budgets and final accounts to enhance transparency. With disclosure as the norm and non-disclosure as the exception, supervise the central government and its departments to disclose budget and final account information in a timely manner according to law, proactively respond to issues of general public concern, and accept social supervision.

II. Strengthening oversight of central budget preparation. Adhere to the principles of having the budget first, then expenditures, and strictly implementing expenditures according to the budget; refine the budget and prepare it in advance. Complete the entire central budget draft within the time limits prescribed by the Budget Law. The central budget shall, in accordance with the Constitution and laws, implement state policies, decisions, and arrangements, ensuring clear policies, scientific standards, and reasonable arrangements, and enhancing readability and auditability.
The draft central general public budget shall include statements on budget revenue and expenditure, transfer payment budgets, basic construction expenditure statements, and government debt statements, and shall explain the budget revenue and expenditure arrangements and the performance targets for transfer payments. The draft central government-managed fund budget shall be prepared and explained separately for each fund item. Government-managed fund expenditures shall be itemized to specific projects for the use of funds, explaining carry-over balances and performance targets. The draft central state capital management budget shall have revenues itemized by industry or enterprise, explaining the overall operating financial status of the previous year for the enterprise units included in the budget; expenditures shall be itemized by use direction and purpose, explaining the basis for project arrangements and performance targets. The draft central social insurance fund budget shall be prepared by insurance item, reflecting the progress of national pooling of basic old-age insurance and explaining the sustainable operation of social insurance funds.

III. Strengthening and improving the preliminary review of the central budget. The fiscal department of the State Council shall promptly inform the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee of the National People's Congress and the Budget Affairs Commission of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of the situation concerning the preparation of the central budget. The Budget Affairs Commission shall, based on listening to the opinions and suggestions of deputies to the National People's Congress and all sectors of society, closely communicate with the fiscal and other departments of the State Council, and study and propose an analysis report on the annual budget. Forty-five days before the convening of the session of the National People's Congress, the fiscal department of the State Council shall submit the preliminary plan of the central budget draft to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee, which shall conduct a preliminary review of the preliminary plan of the central budget draft, carry out special deliberation on relevant key issues, and put forward preliminary review opinions.
During the preliminary review stage conducted by the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee, the relevant special committees of the National People's Congress shall, focusing on state policies, decisions, and arrangements, conduct special reviews of the preliminary plans of departmental budgets in related fields, transfer payment funds, and policies, and put forward special review opinions. In the special review opinions, suggestions to increase relevant expenditure budgets shall be put forward simultaneously with suggestions to reduce other expenditure budgets, so as to maintain the balance, completeness, and unity of the budget. The special review opinions of the relevant special committees shall be sent to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee and the Budget Affairs Commission for study and processing, and when necessary, shall be attached to the preliminary review opinions and distributed at the session of the National People's Congress.

IV. Strengthening oversight of central budget implementation. Under the leadership of the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee, the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee and the Budget Affairs Commission shall perform relevant duties. The relevant departments of the State Council shall promptly submit to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee and the Budget Affairs Commission the situation concerning the implementation of the budget resolution of the National People's Congress. The fiscal department of the State Council shall regularly provide statements on the implementation of the national, central, and local budgets, reflecting the budget revenues and expenditures, government debt, and other relevant information. The relevant departments of the State Council shall, through platforms such as the national e-government network, regularly provide policy systems and data information on departmental budget implementation, macroeconomics, finance, audit, taxation, customs, social security, and state-owned assets.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall strengthen oversight of the implementation of key revenue and expenditure policies, the allocation and use of fiscal funds in key areas, major fiscal and tax reforms and policy adjustments, and the implementation of major investment projects through means such as hearing and deliberating special work reports, law enforcement inspections, and special research. In August each year, the State Council shall report to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the budget implementation for that year. The fiscal department of the State Council and relevant competent departments shall provide, on a quarterly basis, information on budget implementation, the implementation of relevant policies, and the progress of key projects.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall use modern information technology to carry out online budget oversight, improve the efficiency of budget review and oversight, and achieve networked and intelligent budget review and oversight. Issues discovered through online budget oversight shall be communicated to the relevant departments of the State Council in a timely manner, and the relevant departments shall verify, handle, and report on the handling situation.

V. Strengthening the review of central budget adjustment plans. During the implementation of the central budget, reductions in expenditures in key areas such as agriculture, education, science and technology, and social security, new issuance of special government bonds, and increases in the scale of local government borrowing shall be subject to review and approval by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. If a budget adjustment must be made during the implementation of the central budget, the State Council shall prepare a central budget adjustment plan, generally submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress between June and October of the current year. Strictly control budget transfers. Budget expenditures of each department and unit shall be implemented according to the budget. If a transfer is truly necessary due to major matters, it shall be handled strictly in accordance with the prescribed procedures. If important policy measures to increase fiscal revenues or expenditures are introduced during the implementation of the central budget, funds are transferred into the National Social Security Fund, or significant changes occur in the structure of budget revenues and expenditures, the fiscal department of the State Council shall promptly inform the Budget Affairs Commission. The Budget Affairs Commission shall promptly inform the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee of the relevant situation, and when necessary, report to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress.

VI. Strengthening the review of central final accounts. The draft central final accounts shall be prepared in accordance with the headings listed in the budget approved by the National People's Congress, showing separately the budgeted figures, adjusted budget figures, and actual final account figures, and explanations shall be provided for significant changes. General public budget expenditures shall be itemized by functional classification to the item level and by economic nature to the section level. Government-managed fund budget expenditures, state capital management budget expenditures, and social insurance fund budget expenditures shall be itemized by functional classification to the item level. Specific matters for which the accrual basis is applied pursuant to the regulations of the State Council shall be reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress before the review of the draft central final accounts. The draft central final accounts shall be submitted to the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee thirty days before the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress meets for review and approval, and the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee shall conduct a preliminary review in conjunction with the audit work report.

VII. Strengthening the review and oversight of budget performance. All departments and units shall implement comprehensive budget performance management, strengthen pre-performance evaluation, strictly manage performance targets, improve the budget performance indicator system, and enhance the quality of performance evaluation. Strengthen the application of performance evaluation results, promote the integration of performance evaluation results with policy improvement, budget arrangement, and management enhancement, advance the disclosure of budget performance information, and submit important performance evaluation results together with the draft final accounts to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for review. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall strengthen the review and oversight of performance targets and performance evaluation results of key expenditures and major projects. When necessary, hold budget performance hearings.

VIII. Strengthening audit oversight of central budget implementation and final accounts. Audit institutions shall, in accordance with the requirements of truthfulness, legality, and efficiency, conduct audit oversight of the implementation of the central budget and other fiscal revenues and expenditures, as well as the draft final accounts, and provide support services for the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress in conducting budget implementation and final account review and oversight. The State Council shall, in June of each year, submit to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress an audit work report on the implementation of the central budget and other fiscal revenues and expenditures for the previous year. The audit work report shall focus on reporting the audit of the previous year's central budget implementation and draft final accounts, the implementation of important policies, and the performance of fiscal funds, comprehensively and objectively reflect the problems found in the audit, reveal the causes of the problems, and put forward suggestions for improving work. The problems found in the audit shall be corrected and handled according to law, the application of audit results shall be strengthened, accountability shall be reinforced, the working mechanism for rectifying problems found in audits shall be improved, and the mechanism for disclosing rectification information shall be perfected. When necessary, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may adopt a resolution on the audit work report.

IX. Strengthening oversight of the rectification of problems found in audits. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall conduct follow-up oversight of the rectification of prominent problems found in audits. It shall comprehensively use methods such as hearing and deliberating special work reports and special inquiries to carry out follow-up oversight, increase oversight intensity, enhance oversight effectiveness, promote the establishment and improvement of a long-term rectification mechanism, and improve the budget management system. Strengthen the connection and coordination mechanism between the National People's Congress's budget review and oversight, disciplinary inspection and supervision, and audit supervision, enhance information sharing, and form a joint oversight force.
The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall, in December of each year, hear and deliberate the report of the State Council on the rectification of problems found in audits. It may, as needed, hear individual rectification reports from the responsible departments and units for prominent problems found in audits. The responsible persons of the relevant departments and units shall attend the meeting to hear opinions and answer inquiries. The rectification report submitted by the State Council shall correspond to the problems revealed and suggestions made in the audit work report, focus on reflecting the rectification of prominent problems found in audits, and provide individual rectification results for prominent problems found in audits and a list of rectification situations for problems found in the audit of central department budget implementation. When necessary, the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress may adopt a resolution on the report on the rectification of problems found in audits.

X. Implementing the filing system and strengthening budget legal liability according to law. The State Council shall promptly file with the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress the following: regulations and normative documents concerning budgets; the division of revenue and expenditure items between the central and local budgets; specific measures for local governments' revenue contributions to the central government and the central government's tax rebates or transfer payments to local governments; summaries of budgets and final accounts submitted by the governments of provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government to the State Council for filing; the comprehensive financial report of the central government; and other matters that shall be filed.
For problems discovered by the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress during budget and final account review and oversight, the relevant organs, departments, units, and localities shall promptly study and handle them. Where laws such as the Budget Law are violated, legal liability shall be pursued according to law. If disciplinary sanctions are required, the relevant working bodies of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress shall promptly notify the supervisory authorities.

XI. Better leveraging the role of deputies to the National People's Congress. The fiscal and other departments of the State Council shall, through methods such as symposiums, briefing sessions, special research, handling of proposals and suggestions, and inviting deputies to the National People's Congress for inspections, earnestly listen to the opinions and suggestions of deputies to the National People's Congress during the processes of budget preparation, policy formulation, and reform promotion, and proactively respond to the concerns of deputies to the National People's Congress. The relevant special committees of the National People's Congress and the relevant working bodies of the Standing Committee shall strengthen communication and contact with deputies to the National People's Congress to better leverage their role. Improve the working mechanism for contacting deputies in budget review.

XII. Duties of the Budget Affairs Commission. The Budget Affairs Commission is a working body of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress, assisting the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee in undertaking specific work on the review of budgets and final accounts, the review of budget adjustment plans, and the oversight of budget implementation by the National People's Congress and its Standing Committee; undertaking specific work on the oversight of the management of state-owned assets and the follow-up oversight of the rectification of prominent problems found in audits; undertaking specific work on online oversight of budgets and state-owned assets; entrusted by the Council of Chairpersons, undertaking the drafting of relevant legal drafts, and assisting the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee in undertaking specific work on the deliberation of relevant legal drafts; and undertaking other specific matters concerning fiscal budgets as provided for in this Decision, as assigned by the Standing Committee and the Council of Chairpersons, and as needed by the Financial and Economic Affairs Committee. With the consent of the Council of Chairpersons, the Budget Affairs Commission may request relevant government departments and units to provide budget information and obtain relevant information, materials, and explanations. With the approval of the Council of Chairpersons, it may investigate the use of budget funds and special funds by various departments, budget units, and major construction projects, and the relevant government departments and units shall actively assist and cooperate.
This Decision shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
